image_description: A beige and brown minibus parked on a paved street with buildings in the background. The vehicle features a boxy shape, large windshield, side windows, and visible wheels. There is text on the front destination board and side panels.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle clearly exhibits a compact, boxy silhouette distinct from full-size coaches, with sufficient height for passenger accommodation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large front windshield and multiple side windows are clearly visible along the passenger compartment.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle has significant height relative to its width, and a sliding door mechanism is visible on the side near the front/mid-section.
A sliding door track and panel are visible on the side of the bus.
The short hood ahead of the windshield indicates a front-engine layout typical of this class of vehicle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the vehicle is occluded by the viewing angle; only the side and front are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White, yellow, or company livery paint with route markings.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bus features a two-tone beige and brown livery with red stripe details, consistent with commercial transport markings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wheels appear proportional to a light commercial vehicle/minibus chassis.
The window configuration and overall size align with the capacity constraints of a minibus.

artifact_observations.location: Front destination sign and side panel text
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the destination header and side panels is illegible and distorted, resembling AI-generated pseudo-text rather than clear characters.
The front grille and bumper lack defined structural edges; they appear melted into the headlight assembly and the lower body panel, lacking realistic mechanical separation.
The front wheel appears slightly elliptical and the contact patch with the ground is soft/blurry, suggesting minor geometric instability in the wheel rendering.
The side mirror lacks a clear reflection or distinct housing structure, appearing as a smooth, featureless blob fused to the door frame.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific vehicle class and distinguish it from similar categories like vans or full-size buses.
To rigorously analyze the legibility and structure of the text artifacts observed on the bus exterior.
To verify if the melted appearance of the front end is a topological error (fusion of parts) or just low resolution.
To check for spatial grounding errors where the wheels meet the pavement and ensure the chassis sits correctly in 3D space.

focus_areas: Text legibility on destination board and side panels
Structural integrity of front bumper/grille assembly
Wheel geometry and ground contact points
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the front grille area; does the topology auditor confirm fusion between the bumper and headlights? Does the text auditor confirm that the lettering is nonsensical/gibberish rather than just blurry? Check if the wheel distortion is a perspective artifact or a generation failure.
